requirements.requirement: Run one four-member distributed MinIO service across node1 through node4 using the dedicated storage network.
requirements.summary: Storage aliases resolve to the four 10.100.125.x addresses, the service configuration uses all four TLS storage endpoints, and direct administration reports one EC:2 pool with all four members and drives online.

requirements.requirement: Provide authenticated TLS S3 access on port 9000.
requirements.summary: All four endpoints listen on port 9000, pass certificate verification, and return healthy cluster status. An unauthenticated object request receives S3 AccessDenied while authenticated mc access reads the object.

requirements.requirement: Create bucket infra-data with proof.txt containing distributed-storage-ready.
requirements.summary: Direct bucket listing, metadata, and object reads show infra-data/proof.txt as a 25-byte object with exactly the requested content.

requirements.requirement: Provide MinIO Client administration from node1.
requirements.summary: On node1, mc configured an authenticated alias and successfully returned administrative information for all four members and the EC:2 pool.

requirements.requirement: Keep objects readable and writable while one storage member is unavailable.
requirements.summary: A healthy four-drive baseline was observed, node4 was stopped with no port-9000 listener, and the degraded three-member cluster directly read proof.txt, wrote degraded-write.txt, and read the new object back.

requirements.requirement: Automatically rejoin the returned member with current data.
requirements.summary: After only restarting node4's service, it became healthy and the cluster returned to four online drives. Although the outage-time object was briefly unavailable through node4 during convergence, subsequent checks showed its local metadata and successful reads of both objects through node4.

overall_summary: All material outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence, including a complete healthy-baseline, single-member disruption, degraded read/write, restoration, and recovered-state transition.
limitations: The disruption stopped the MinIO service on node4; it did not simulate a full host power loss or storage-network partition.
No reboot test was captured, although service enablement and persistent mount configuration support restart persistence.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final snapshots show no failed services and healthy dpkg state on all nodes. Minor residue remains: three executor-created test files under /tmp on node1 and the outage-test object remains in the bucket. No final service conflict or package damage is evident.
